minimal_symbolic_certificate.structured_equivalent: first_failing_gate_index J in {1,2,3,4,5,⊥}; when J!=⊥ outcome=CJ_REJECT and K is not-applicable; when J=⊥, K=0 gives C6_UNRESOLVED and K=1 gives C6_PASS
minimal_symbolic_certificate.derived_H: H=1 iff J!=⊥; H=0 iff J=⊥
minimal_symbolic_certificate.cardinality_minimality: The frozen taxonomy has seven mutually exclusive outcomes, so any lossless certificate needs at least seven distinct valid values. The tagged union has exactly seven valid values and is cardinality-minimal. Any fixed-width binary representation therefore needs at least ceil(log2(7))=3 bits.

losslessness_proof.H_K_J: Lossless under the stated validity constraints: J=1..5 decodes uniquely to C1..C5 respectively; J=⊥ with H=0 and K=0 decodes to C6_UNRESOLVED; J=⊥ with H=0 and K=1 decodes to C6_PASS. Thus all seven outcomes have distinct valid certificates. H is redundant because it is derivable from J.
losslessness_proof.H_K_only: Insufficient for branch-specific diagnosis. Under the frozen classifier every C1-C5 rejection has H=1, so dropping J collapses distinct first-failing branches. Even if an implementation retained both K values during rejection, {H,K} offers at most two H=1 codes for five reject branches; by pigeonhole at least two branches collide. Therefore {H,K} cannot losslessly reconstruct the seven-outcome taxonomy or identify the first failing gate.
losslessness_proof.minimal_field_form: A single seven-valued outcome tag is information-equivalent and field-minimal; the gate-structured minimal form is {J,K} with K defined only for J=⊥. Adding H improves readability/checking but not information content.

certificate_validity_invariants: No certificate with H=1,J=⊥ or H=0,J in {1..5} is valid
